indicators: Unusually large gradient values in model update payloads (e.g., > 10x expected magnitude)
Frequent rejection of updates from a specific client node by model aggregator
Abnormal spikes in model loss or sudden drops in accuracy after aggregation rounds involving suspicious clients
Server logs showing warnings about gradient anomalies tied to specific client IDs
Network traffic POST requests to /federated/update with suspicious payload hashes
examples.detection_method: Implement anomaly detection on gradient updates by calculating statistical deviation (e.g., z-score) of submitted gradients per layer and per client. Flag updates exceeding defined thresholds. Monitor model performance metrics after each aggregation round for sudden degradation. Correlate server logs for repeated gradient anomaly warnings from the same client. Use cryptographic signatures to verify client authenticity and detect replay or tampering attempts.
